dedupe_keys.name: climate resilience demonstrator credo connected digital twin of energy water and telecoms under flooding

description: CReDo is a UK climate change adaptation digital twin project that shows how connected data can improve resilience across a system of systems. It looks at the impact of flooding on energy, water and telecoms networks: Anglian Water, BT and UK Power Networks shared asset and operations data, with Met Office weather data, on a secure basis to build a digital twin of the three networks, so that owners and operators could see how failures cascade across sector boundaries and coordinate capital, operational and real-time decisions. The first phase was delivered by the Universities of Cambridge, Edinburgh, Newcastle and Warwick, the Science and Technology Facilities Council and the Joint Centre of Excellence in Environmental Intelligence, funded by BEIS, Connected Places Catapult and the University of Cambridge; Connected Places Catapult now leads its next stage. UK Power Networks' follow-on CReDO+ (October 2023 to March 2028, budget about 10.9 million pounds under the Strategic Innovation Fund) extends the platform with probabilistic failure models for extreme heat, wind and flooding and with economic and societal cost data. The project pages and an interactive visualisation are accessible online as free HTML on the Digital Twin Hub; the utilities' underlying data are not public. Caveats: the demonstrator covers one region's networks and its results are reported at summary level. It illustrates digital twin simulation of cascading failure and climate adaptation across infrastructure interdependencies; related records are NISMOD and DAFNI.
